summary: Revise at 5.0 (author 6.0; Caiman 7; ship needs 7.5). The export build is clean and the template lifts with 0 patches. Two release gates are red, and the ring does not read as Odin's ravens. At 300 px it reads as a black cab in a tall plain collet, with a serpent- or eel-like head lying along the band and biting it. Two heads facing a stone, on a band that runs on out of their mouths, is the double-serpent ring layout. The cause is the composition, which reverses the plan. Each beak (stamps at θ 53.3° and 126.9°) points at the stone from the middle of its own arm. Each arm therefore runs on about 55° past its bird's beak, under the stone, as a blank polished slab. The slab ends in the bypass tip's step right under the other bird's beak (tips at θ 55° and 125°). In hero and shoulder that step reads as a crack from beak root to bore edge. The plan puts the heads on the arm tips with the beaks pointing outward, which is also how Logan's RavenRing runs its beak down the band. The heads are smooth painted domes whose painted feather lanes (0.1 mm deep at most) render as streaks and a comb along the flanks. The eyes are round craters that read as rivets. The beak stamps stand only 0.07 mm at their edges over a 2.5 mm painted mass, so they read as a lozenge plate, not a mandible. There is no medium-scale feather: the shingles read as rounded tread blocks, the herringbone as a knit or wheat hatch, and the crossing tails as two faint diagonal seams. The hero's near side face and the crossing flanks are bare. The collet shows about 1.5-2 mm of plain stepped wall and outweighs the birds in the hero, whose composition repeats Arachne's black onyx in a plain bezel beside a figure. Gates: everything passes at 1536×448. The draft 768×320 release is Blocked with 1 obstruction at 0.100 mm, and the author's own gate block exits 'Corvus failed its gates' there. The 384×192 run records 1 obstruction at 0.075 mm, 0.063 mm deep, under a stamps_384 flag that does not test release. Ruling: plausibly crest-row phantoms, not proven; the gate is not met and not waived. Another round is worth it: this is the collection's only two-creature bypass, with real sculptural mass, a lean 1.09 MB graph and a clean export.
strengths: The concept uses the bypass structurally: each arm is one bird, and this is the collection's only two-creature ring. Nothing on it is foreign: heads, beaks, plumage, tails and graver work are all raven by intent.
The ring has real sculptural mass. The heads stand about 2.9 mm proud (r ≈ 15.1 mm against a 12.26 mm crest), so the side view carries two shoulder masses, a profile no other Bestiarium ring has.
The palm herringbone is the densest small-scale work on the ring and reads as fine plumage in full-size close-ups.
The author's self-review was honest (smooth heads, the far-head lump, the stone-heavy hero, the weak 300 px read), and it reported the draft and 384 release hits instead of hiding them.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Every zone is raven by intent: heads and beaks at the top, plumage down both shoulders, tails at the palm, graver barbs throughout. Nothing comes from outside the subject. Caveat: the 'Onyx nest' smear and the two blank arm runs beside the collet belong to no bird, and they sit in the most-viewed zone.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines (stamps, parts, or crisp painted relief with no combing, smearing or stair-steps)
checklist.reason:
- The beak stamps are true outlines, but they stand only 0.07 mm at their edges (height_mm 0.07, gable rise 0.38) over a painted beak 2.5 mm deep. The outline barely registers, and the beak reads as a lozenge plate.
- The heads are painted domes. The skull's painted 'feathered' lanes (0.1 mm deep at most) render as streaks and a comb along the flanks in side.png.
- The crossing tails at the palm are faint diagonal seams, not feathers.
- The shoulder shingles read as rounded rectangular blocks.

checklist.item: Faces and eyes read well (a poor face is a defect)
checklist.reason: The skulls are smooth rounded masses with none of a raven's markers: no culmen-to-crown step, no flat crown, no nasal bristles, no throat hackles. The bench-cut eyes are round craters with a raised centre (a Cone top), and they read as rivets or bolt holes in hero.png and side.png. From the hero angle the far head reads as a lump, as the author concedes.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The 8 × 6 onyx sits in a made bezel collet (1,728 faces, closed, 0 crossings) and is clearly visible. The stones report and the preview each count 1. The collet is soldered after the pour, and the pattern carries its drill dot. The collet itself is plain and tall: see checklist 6 and punch item 5.

checklist.item: Shoulder ornament is not cut off toward the face
checklist.reason: Plumage stops at each head, and the beak tips stop at the collet. Beyond each beak, its own arm runs on as a bare polished slab past the stone: arm A over θ ≈ 70-125°, arm B over θ ≈ 55-110°. Each slab ends in the bypass tip's step under the other bird's beak (θ 55° and 125°). In hero.png and shoulder.png that step is a straight line from beak root to bore edge, and it reads as a crack.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason:
- stones.png: a tall cylindrical collet with a stepped double rim and about 1.5-2 mm of plain wall.
- face.png: flat polished crossing flanks on either side of the collet.
- shoulder.png and reverse.png: shoulder shingles that read as rounded tread blocks with inset slots.
- hero.png: long straight lines along the band under the near head.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Procedural bypass LowDome 6.0 × 3.0; no factory stock.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Bestiarium rings
checklist.reason: Only partly distinct. The side view's two heavy shoulder masses and the collet box are unlike any other ring in the collection. At 300 px, though, the hero repeats Arachne's composition: a black oval onyx in a plain bezel at left with a figure beside it. The face view reads as a stone flanked by two horns. The bypass crossing, the ring's one structural signature, is not legible.

checklist.item: Reads as its subject at a glance at 300 px, without the caption
checklist.reason: In _contact300.png and _compare300.png the hero reads as a black cab with a serpent- or eel-like head biting it, and the face reads as a cab between two horns. Without the caption nobody would name ravens or count two birds. Heads facing a stone on a band that continues out of their mouths is the double-serpent ring.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large forms (heads) and the small forms (barbs at 0.42 mm pitch) are there, but the medium scale is missing: there are no individual feathers of 1.5-3 mm, and the herringbone reads as hatch. The hero's near side face and the crossing flanks are bare polished metal. For comparison, Caiman reads at plate, knob and granule scale everywhere, and Logan's RavenRing carries chevron feathers about 2 mm wide that read at thumbnail size.

punch_list.zone: Gate block in bestiarium_corvus.rs (the stamps_384 flag at lines 1154-1158 and the report assembly), plus every painted apex on the crest: the primaries' fan apex at θ 285-305° and both heads' crests and foreheads
punch_list.change:
(a) Make stamps_384 require 0 obstructions and 0 unresolved rays at both 0.100 and 0.075 mm.
(b) Write the draft 768×320 release blocks into report.json beside the export and 384 blocks, each with θ, r, z and depth for every obstruction.
(c) Remove the crest-row mechanism by construction:
- Hold every painted apex that sits on the parting line flat along the ring for ±0.3 mm across the crest (CREST_FLAT 0.1 → 0.3 mm in those windows).
- End the primaries' fan before its rays converge on the crest, or move its apex at least 0.5 mm off it.
- Seat painted crests on the interpolated crest (setting::crest_v or Hide::crest_at), not on the nearest atlas row. This is Caiman's rule for anything pointed on the crest.
(d) If a single-cell hit survives and is still called a phantom, attach the true-surface probe or the convergence table from the gate ruling.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json shows 0 obstructions and 0 unresolved rays at both 0.100 and 0.075 mm at 384×192, 768×320 and 1536×448. The draft run exits 0 with gates_passed true, and stamps_384 is true under the tightened definition.

punch_list.zone: Crossing and upper shoulders, θ ≈ 10-170°: stamps 'Huginn, beak' and 'Muninn, beak'; layers 'Raven heads', 'Onyx nest' and 'Raven plumage'
punch_list.change:
Restore the plan's composition. Each bird runs the full length of its arm, with its head at the arm's tip beside the stone and its beak pointing outward ('thought and memory sent out').
- Today's Huginn rides the arm that ends at θ 125°, and his body stays on the θ < 90° shoulder:
  - his neck crosses under the collet;
  - his skull covers θ ≈ 110-135°, its rear against the collet skirt, with the arm's rounded tip under his throat;
  - his beak lies on the parting line from θ ≈ 135° outward, tip no further than θ 170° (flip rot_deg).
- Muninn mirrors him: skull θ ≈ 45-70°, beak θ ≈ 10-45° pointing outward.
- Sizes along the crest: skull 5.0-6.0 mm, beak 6.0-7.2 mm.
- Raise each struck beak's edge from 0.07 mm to 0.30-0.35 mm, with a gable rise of 0.35-0.45 mm. Alternatively use the plan's fallback 2, a Ridge falling toward the tip. Either way the mandible outline must read, and the beak stays parting-monotone.
- Replace the 'Onyx nest' smear on the crossing flanks with the feathers of the two crossed necks, so no polished run longer than 2 mm lies between the collet and a head.
Why: nothing in front of a bird's face can account for the arm running on past its beak. On a bypass, the facing layout will always read as a serpent biting the band.

punch_list.zone: Both skulls and beaks after item 2: layer 'Raven heads', the four eye stamps, and the plumage and graver alphas under the head footprint
punch_list.acceptance:
- A new head.png (a three-quarter close-up of one head at 3× or more the hero scale) shows the beak, forehead step, flat crown and nape dip, the almond eye under its step, and hackles on the side face, with no streaks or comb on the skull.
- side.png shows the beak, forehead, crown and nape silhouette on both heads.
- The field report attributes no undercut to 'Raven heads'.
- DFM stays at 0, and every stamp is resolved and parting-monotone.

punch_list.zone: Bodies from the crossed necks down both shoulders to the palm, on the outer surface and both side faces: layer 'Raven plumage' plus new wing stamps

- In hero.png the near side face has no bare polished run longer than 3 mm between θ 190° and 350°.
